classification.difficultyReason: Integrate a vector acceleration and apply symbolic initial conditions to establish general velocity and position formulas.

content.prompt:
A particle is projected from the origin with speed $V$ at angle $\theta$ above the horizontal. By integrating, show that

$$\mathbf v=(V\cos\theta)\mathbf i+(-10t+V\sin\theta)\mathbf j$$

and

$$\mathbf r=(Vt\cos\theta)\mathbf i+(-5t^2+Vt\sin\theta)\mathbf j.$$

Take $g=10$ m/s².

answer.short: $\mathbf v=(V\cos\theta)\mathbf i+(-10t+V\sin\theta)\mathbf j$ and $\mathbf r=(Vt\cos\theta)\mathbf i+(-5t^2+Vt\sin\theta)\mathbf j$, obtained by integrating $\mathbf a=-10\mathbf j$ and using the initial velocity and $\mathbf r(0)=\mathbf0$.
answer.worked:
$$\mathbf a=0\mathbf i-10\mathbf j$$

$$\begin{aligned}\mathbf v&=\int(0\mathbf i-10\mathbf j)\,dt\\ \mathbf v&=C_1\mathbf i+(-10t+C_2)\mathbf j\\ \mathbf v(0)&=V\cos\theta\mathbf i+V\sin\theta\mathbf j\\ C_1&=V\cos\theta\\ C_2&=V\sin\theta\end{aligned}$$

$$\boxed{\mathbf v=(V\cos\theta)\mathbf i+(-10t+V\sin\theta)\mathbf j}$$

$$\begin{aligned}\mathbf r&=\int\left[(V\cos\theta)\mathbf i+(-10t+V\sin\theta)\mathbf j\right]dt\\ \mathbf r&=(Vt\cos\theta+C_3)\mathbf i\\ &\quad+(-5t^2+Vt\sin\theta+C_4)\mathbf j\\ \mathbf r(0)&=0\mathbf i+0\mathbf j\\ C_3&=0\\ C_4&=0\end{aligned}$$

$$\boxed{\mathbf r=(Vt\cos\theta)\mathbf i+(-5t^2+Vt\sin\theta)\mathbf j}$$

Here $t$ is in seconds, $V$ and $\mathbf v$ are in m/s, and $\mathbf r$ is in metres.
